I rebuilt my resolved trial tree (main + my resolution) and compared it with 74eb343a. The write-refusal threshold stays at 250, and the env ceiling is 250+90. I reran my FakeMeta repro (10 sets × 3 ads × 3 work-position terms, cold cache): budget 330, 252 calls used, success. With 4 terms per set the resolver cap is hit and the run is refused before any write ("press Check plan again"); this is 1771 behaviour. 2 sets × 3 terms: success.
2. **ACL-1891.** `_prepare` refuses before the first write when `chunk_calls + estimate_create_calls(plan) > budget`. Check plan (`writing=False`) keeps the old reserve. The 1891 test is rewritten and a new test is added; the 1891 suite passes.

- **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". The code only checks when there are large-video chunks. For non-video plans, the targeting reserve is the only guard. One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.

# ACL-2945 returned from batch b3c757b9 (PR #1948): duplicate accounts from inner spaces; bad rows get no error

The integration review (Reviewer-R1117Ib3c7) checked head 50b20127f. The composition was exact, and the Home map fix is verified: app.py writes account_links country, and tests assert the Home builder's structure. All 7 Issue criteria have tests; 105 affected tests passed. Three input defects block approval:

1. Inner whitespace creates duplicates. In `src/web/user_assign.py:250-255`, the exact match and `_resolve_new_account`'s `seen[name.lower()]` compare only `strip().lower()`. So "Alpha  1, PE" (two spaces) is added next to the existing "Alpha 1", and "gamma   9, PE" + "GAMMA 9, PE" in one paste add two accounts. Fix: normalise with `" ".join(name.split()).casefold()` for matching and `seen`, and store the collapsed name.
2. A row with an extra part gets no reason. `parse_add_line` returns None for a third non-number part, so "Name, PE, SA" comes back `not_found` with no `error` and the UI shows nothing. Fix: return a clear English error on that row, e.g. "Too many parts. Write: name, PE or name, PE, act_123".
3. Names are not validated. A leading `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is written to ad_account_map.csv as is (spreadsheet formula injection; the owner opens it in Excel). NUL characters and a 400-character name are accepted. Fix: reject control characters and over-long names, and refuse or guard formula-leading names, with an English error. Add a test for each.

Also have the builder's report say whether ad_account_id is filled after Open.

The integration review (Reviewer-R1117I1c3c, Opus) found that criterion 1 ("the second shows no refusal note") fails on one path. The PR head is f2e4930bf (member tip ce51f0e1a = PR #1941 head). The composition was exact.

- `src/fb_api/creator.py` `_prepare`: `reset_targeting_notes()` runs at :5383, after `_require_compressor_for_big_videos` (:5375) and `check_profile_page` (:5382). Both can raise PlanError.
- When campaign B raises there (stop_kind "plan"), `plan_only` still calls `self._audit(...)` (:6009) -> `preflight_rules.server_verdicts` -> `put_resolved` (preflight_rules.py:830-837) reads `resolver.targeting_warnings()`.
- `TermResolver._touched` (targeting_resolver.py, `warnings()` ~:494) still holds campaign A's touches, because no reset ran for B.

Repro with the test fakes (RefusingMeta refusing adworkposition, same account, one creator):
- A ("Qwerty"): warning, audit interests_resolve = warning. Correct.
- B ("Forex", exact match, never touches adworkposition, check_profile_page raises PlanError): out.warnings clean, but audit interests_resolve = warning carrying A's "Meta refused the work positions lookup (adworkposition)" text.
- The same B without the early stop is clean.
- ACL-2932 notes probably leak the same way on this path (inferred from code, not run).

Fix: reset the targeting notes at the top of `_prepare` (before :5375), or in `plan_only` before `_prepare`. Add a test: "B stops with PlanError before the reset; its audit has no refusal from A".

Everything else passed: per-campaign notes on the normal path, cached terms replay their own refusals, no new calls or caching, separate resolver per account, English text, 2925/2932/2938 paths untouched.

# ACL-2945 source review — changes requested

Reviewer-R1126R2945 / rev_1126r_2945. PR #1946 head bd0cbd821, base main 3c02506db (branch is ahead of main, no refresh needed).
CI on bd0cbd821: green (linux 1-3, windows, ACL verification, tracker-link).
Affected tests (2945 + 2924/2920/2900/2899, temp config dir): 81 passed.

## Blocking

1. **"Name, PE" for an account that is on the shared accounts list but not in this machine's map is NOT added to the map.**
   `src/web/user_assign.py:206` (`names` includes `sheet_labels`), `:216` (`match()`) and `:242` (`candidates, partial, _ = match(add["name"])`).
   The shared-list label wins, the line becomes plain `found` with an empty row (`entry is None`), the country is dropped, `/api/user-assign/send` adds nothing, and Check shows "Found", not "Will be added to Peru".
   Probe: `resolve_lines(["Sheet Only, PE"], {}, ["Sheet Only"])` -> `state=found`, `country=None`, row country "".
   This fails criteria 1 and 2 ("an account that is not in the map" -> "Will be added to Peru", and after Assign it is in `ad_account_map.csv` under its country). The test fixture patches `fetch_account_rows` to `[]`, so no test covers it.
   Fix: for a line with a country code, treat the account as existing only if its name is an exact (case-insensitive) key of `account_map`; otherwise go to `_resolve_new_account` (state `add`). Add a test with a shared-list label.

## Non-blocking (please fix while there)

2. Partial-name match beats an explicit add: `"Acme, PE"` with `Acme Peru 2` in the map -> `found`, `match=partial`, assigns the existing account (`user_assign.py:242`). Visible on Check as "Matched by part of the name", but a line that names a country is an explicit "new account" — consider exact-only matching for the add form (same fix as 1).
3. Add succeeded, hub assign failed (`src/web/app.py:4283-4284`): the rows are already in the map but `sent` is unset, so `user_assign.js:102` still labels them "Will be added to Peru". Retrying works (they are then `found`), but the label is wrong after the failure; say "Added to Peru" (not assigned) for names in `added`.
4. `"Name, 123"` -> reason `Unknown country code "".` (empty code; `user_assign.py:274`). Say "No country code" instead.
5. CSV formula injection: a name like `=HYPERLINK(...)` is written as-is to `ad_account_map.csv` (`app.py:4266-4272` -> `account_map_patch`). Pre-existing in the manual add path too, so low; optional guard on leading `= + - @`.

## Checked and fine
- Write path reuses `/account-map-patch` handler: `config.paths.get_ad_account_map_path()`, `write_csv_atomic`, keeps all existing columns, case-insensitive upsert by name (no duplicate rows; test `the_second_assign...`), clash check, buyer tag, un-hide.
- Country spelling: map's existing spelling preferred, else title-cased `country_names` entry (PE->Peru, SA->Saudi Arabia, GB->United Kingdom).
- Add failure -> that line only becomes Not found with the handler's error (`app.py:4276`).
- No add happens when the buyer email is missing (target check runs first).
- Accounts already in the map: unchanged, map untouched (test).
- No new buttons/timers/banners; UI text English.

operation.report:
# ACL-2945 returned from batch b3c757b9 (PR #1948): duplicate accounts from inner spaces; bad rows get no error

The integration review (Reviewer-R1117Ib3c7) checked head 50b20127f. The composition was exact, and the Home map fix is verified: app.py writes account_links country, and tests assert the Home builder's structure. All 7 Issue criteria have tests; 105 affected tests passed. Three input defects block approval:

1. Inner whitespace creates duplicates. In `src/web/user_assign.py:250-255`, the exact match and `_resolve_new_account`'s `seen[name.lower()]` compare only `strip().lower()`. So "Alpha  1, PE" (two spaces) is added next to the existing "Alpha 1", and "gamma   9, PE" + "GAMMA 9, PE" in one paste add two accounts. Fix: normalise with `" ".join(name.split()).casefold()` for matching and `seen`, and store the collapsed name.
2. A row with an extra part gets no reason. `parse_add_line` returns None for a third non-number part, so "Name, PE, SA" comes back `not_found` with no `error` and the UI shows nothing. Fix: return a clear English error on that row, e.g. "Too many parts. Write: name, PE or name, PE, act_123".
3. Names are not validated. A leading `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is written to ad_account_map.csv as is (spreadsheet formula injection; the owner opens it in Excel). NUL characters and a 400-character name are accepted. Fix: reject control characters and over-long names, and refuse or guard formula-leading names, with an English error. Add a test for each.

Also have the builder's report say whether ad_account_id is filled after Open.

src/web/user_assign.py:192 (parse_add_line takes parts[0] as the name unconditionally) and

an English reason, e.g. "The name looks like an ad account number. Write the account as: name, PE, act_…".

## 2. Blocking: invisible / C1 control characters pass the name check and make look-alike duplicates
src/web/user_assign.py:209-211 (norm_name only collapses str.split() whitespace) and :225
(control check is only ord < 32 or 127).

# ACL-2950 review (Reviewer-R1127R2950) — changes requested

PR #1951 head 350c301d2, base main 036f92d65 (branch is `ahead`). PR CI green (linux 1-3, windows, tracker-link, process, ACL verification). Affected tests pass locally (135: 2950, 2899, 2901, 2915, 2945, 2920). All Issue checkboxes are covered by tests. The blocker below is a regression of existing Home actions that every real sync hits.

## Blocking

1. **When a buyer removes a hub account from a country by hand (Home unlink, or Close country), the next sync puts it back.**
   `src/web/user_accounts.py:345-371` (`place_countries`) treats "has no country link now" as "never placed". It runs on every sync, 304 included. Home calls the sync on every page open and every time the tab becomes visible (`src/web/static/user_accounts_sync.js:20,37`).
   - `unlink` leaves only a placeholder row (`account_links.py` `unlink`).
   - `close_country` removes the rows (`account_links.py` `close_country`).

   In both cases the map still carries the hub country, so the account is linked again and the closed country comes back.

   Reproducer, same fixtures as `tests/test_acl2950_sync_country_links.py`:
   ```python
   hub = Hub([acc("Alpha", country="Peru")]); run(hub)
   account_links.unlink("Alpha", "country", "Peru")
   run(hub)  # 304 -> {'status': 'not_modified', 'changed': True, 'placed': 1}; links == [('Alpha','Peru')] again
   hub = Hub([acc("A", country="Peru"), acc("B", country="Peru")]); run(hub)
   account_links.close_country("country", "Peru")
   run(hub)  # placed 2; Peru is back with A and B
   ```
   So the Home "take out" and "Close" actions no longer work for any hub-assigned account. The buyer's own action is undone silently.

   Suggested fix: sync places each account only once. Keep the keys of accounts that sync has already handled, for example a `placed` list in the user_accounts state file. Skip those keys on later syncs. Catch-up still works, because that set is empty on the first sync after release. Add a test for each of unlink and close.

## Non-blocking notes

2. **Write storm and lost updates.** `place_countries` calls `account_links.link` once per account (`user_accounts.py:361`). Each call loads the whole file, rewrites it, fsyncs it and replaces it.
   - 300 accounts took 3.0 s on the first catch-up sync on this laptop. A 304 with nothing to do takes 6 ms.
   - Neither `account_links.link` nor the sync holds a lock against Home actions. In a reproducer, a Home `link` thread ran during a 100-account catch-up sync:
     - 12 of 17 Home links that returned True were lost.
     - 3 Home links raised PermissionError (file being replaced).
     - 10 sync links were lost even though the sync reported them as placed. The next sync recovers those.

   The race existed before this PR, but the sync is a new background writer. Suggestion: compute all new rows and write them once, through one load and one `_write`. This also shrinks the race window. Also consider a module lock in account_links.
3. A links file that cannot be decoded (corrupt bytes) is caught by the outer `except`. The sync result has no `place_notes` entry, only a log line. Acceptable.
4. Spelling: "UAE" does not join an "AE" or "United Arab Emirates" group. `_known_code` has no "uae" alias, which comes from the ACL-2945 table. A lowercase map spelling ("ua", "saudi arabia") becomes the group's display name when no group exists yet. Both follow the spec.
5. `place_countries` creates `account_links.csv` when it is missing. After that, `account_links.seed_from_account_map()`, which runs lazily from Home, skips the seed because the file exists. Manual map countries on a machine that never opened Home would not be seeded. This is an edge case.
6. Accounts the buyer removed from the Available accounts list (`available_hidden.csv`, ACL-1319) are still placed under their country. Only `hidden_accounts.json` is respected. Minor.

## Verified OK
- Name variants (double spaces, case, Cf characters) match an existing placement.
- A hand link to another country is kept.
- Sync-hidden and hand-hidden accounts are skipped.
- Empty, unknown and unusable countries behave as described.
- A read-only links file gives per-account notes and the sync is still ok.
- A missing map leaves the sync ok.
- After 40 mixed accounts and three syncs (200, 304, new etag), the file is byte-identical and its mtime unchanged.
- The 2899/2901/2915 fixtures now patch `account_links.get_local_config_dir`. No test that references user_accounts lacks the patch.
- The real files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ACL and in the \localhost path were unchanged (size and mtime) before and after.

   src/fb_ads_rpa/failure_policy.py:108-116 ("a partial draft may be left in Ads Manager"), :131-137 ("the draft
   already exists when the objective is checked inside the single-screen editor"), tests/fixtures/ads_manager/README.md:125
   (the captured editor carried campaign/ad set/ad object ids). The driver only closes the tab (page_backed_ui.py:150-155),
   so every attempt - including every refused one ("another Page", timeouts), multiplied by finding 1 - can leave a
   draft campaign. Either discard the draft safely, or get an explicit owner decision that a leftover draft is accepted
   and change the changelog/docstring ("closed without saving") accordingly.

3. **Wrong landing is a deny-list, not detection.** `_bad_page` (page_backed_ui.py:116) rejects only login/checkpoint,
   `selected_ad_ids` and `/ads/edit`. It accepts `/campaigns/edit`, `/adsets/edit`, `selected_campaign_ids` /

1629.review_report:
# ACL-2629 review round 4 - head b4d2269e2 - RETURNED

Tests (from C:/acl-2629, one file at a time): test_acl2629_worker_upload 77 passed, test_acl1891_video_chunks 55, test_acl1756_page_helper_node 23, test_acl2000_video_compress_resume 9. acl_scan_secrets: clean.

## Blocking

B1. Network.setBypassServiceWorker on the ordinary Ads Manager page session is never reverted.
`UploadServer.arm()` (src/fb_api/upload_server.py:108-113) sets `{"bypass": True}` on the page session of a normal
(non-light) tab; `disarm()` (lines 193-209) turns off auto-attach and Fetch but does not send `{"bypass": False}`.
The controller's CDP session stays attached to Meta's tab for the whole profile session, so whatever this setting does
stays on Meta's own page after the upload. Fix: in `disarm()`, for a non-light tab, send
`Network.setBypassServiceWorker {"bypass": false}` (best effort, `_note` on error), and add a test that arm/disarm leave
the page session's bypass as it was (only worker sessions may keep it, and they are detached).

B2. Inline mode is not fail-closed against a service worker; the bypass that is meant to protect it does nothing here.
The repo's own verified note (src/fb_ads_rpa/light_probe.py:6-7, 90) says `setBypassServiceWorker` has no effect
without `Network.enable`, and `Network.enable` is banned by a test in `src/fb_api`. So on an ordinary tab whose document is
controlled by a Meta service worker, inline piece fetches (`https://adsmanager.facebook.com/__acl_upload/<serve token>/<o>/<n>`)
go to the SW's fetch handler first. The SW's own fetch is a separate target that the page session's Fetch pattern does not
catch, so the request reaches Meta's servers. Nothing leaks: no cookies (`credentials: 'omit'`), no file bytes, a non-200
reply is refused. But Meta sees an unusual GET with our serve token from a live account, and the inline probe fails
quietly. Design note section 11 says "A service worker is bypassed", which is not true for this code.
Fix: before any piece fetch, `runInline` (and preferably the worker path, whose blob worker is controlled by the same SW) refuses with
`no_worker: 'page controlled by a service worker'` when `navigator.serviceWorker && navigator.serviceWorker.controller`.
That way the run falls back to compression and the diagnostics name it. Alternatively, prove the bypass works without
Network.enable on a local SW and add that test. Fix the design note either way.

## Checked, fine
- (a) Freeze: no base64/atob in the page. Each piece is `fetch` -> `blob()` -> `arrayBuffer()` (one 8 MB copy, async) ->
  `crypto.subtle.digest` (async, off the main thread in Chrome) -> kept as Blob. `new Blob(parts)` and FormData only
  hold references, and the POST body streams from blob storage. Main-thread sync work per chunk is a 32-byte hex and a
  little object glue. Memory in flight: at most one chunk (64 MB of Blobs) plus one 8 MB ArrayBuffer, with one call at a
  time per helper. Fulfil bodies are decoded in the browser process, not on the renderer main thread. No freeze risk found.
- (d) Diagnostics: counts, error class names, error text cut to 80-100 chars, CSP directive plus 20 chars of blockedURI
  (`blob:https://adsmana`). No act ids, access tokens or full URLs. The serve token is not in the trace.
- (e) Policy parity: inline goes through the same `runInWorker` entry and the same `makeRunner.run` (same fields,
  `redirect: 'error'`, referrer, piece deadline, size and hash check, abort through `inlineRunner.abort`). The probe makes no
  POST (`!m.url`). Disarm runs in `finally` for the probe and for transfers. Python: offset and policy checks did not change.
- (f) Merge of main fedcb9177: the only src change in the merge is src/web (flags/home table). The ACL-2611/2621/2618
  areas (creator/write_policy/light_tab) carry only this PR's lines, and the four test files pass.

## Non-blocking
- `import sys` added to upload_server.py is unused.
- `disarm()`'s worker-detach loop still uses `self.errors += 1` instead of `_note(exc)`, so its error is missing from the
  trace.

# ACL-2950 review (Reviewer-R1127R2950) — changes requested

PR #1951 head 350c301d2, base main 036f92d65 (branch is `ahead`). PR CI green (linux 1-3, windows, tracker-link, process, ACL verification). Affected tests pass locally (135: 2950, 2899, 2901, 2915, 2945, 2920). All Issue checkboxes are covered by tests. The blocker below is a regression of existing Home actions that every real sync hits.

## Blocking

1. **When a buyer removes a hub account from a country by hand (Home unlink, or Close country), the next sync puts it back.**
   `src/web/user_accounts.py:345-371` (`place_countries`) treats "has no country link now" as "never placed". It runs on every sync, 304 included. Home calls the sync on every page open and every time the tab becomes visible (`src/web/static/user_accounts_sync.js:20,37`).
   - `unlink` leaves only a placeholder row (`account_links.py` `unlink`).
   - `close_country` removes the rows (`account_links.py` `close_country`).

   In both cases the map still carries the hub country, so the account is linked again and the closed country comes back.

   Reproducer, same fixtures as `tests/test_acl2950_sync_country_links.py`:
   ```python
   hub = Hub([acc("Alpha", country="Peru")]); run(hub)
   account_links.unlink("Alpha", "country", "Peru")
   run(hub)  # 304 -> {'status': 'not_modified', 'changed': True, 'placed': 1}; links == [('Alpha','Peru')] again
   hub = Hub([acc("A", country="Peru"), acc("B", country="Peru")]); run(hub)
   account_links.close_country("country", "Peru")
   run(hub)  # placed 2; Peru is back with A and B
   ```
   So the Home "take out" and "Close" actions no longer work for any hub-assigned account. The buyer's own action is undone silently.

   Suggested fix: sync places each account only once. Keep the keys of accounts that sync has already handled, for example a `placed` list in the user_accounts state file. Skip those keys on later syncs. Catch-up still works, because that set is empty on the first sync after release. Add a test for each of unlink and close.

## Non-blocking notes

2. **Write storm and lost updates.** `place_countries` calls `account_links.link` once per account (`user_accounts.py:361`). Each call loads the whole file, rewrites it, fsyncs it and replaces it.
   - 300 accounts took 3.0 s on the first catch-up sync on this laptop. A 304 with nothing to do takes 6 ms.
   - Neither `account_links.link` nor the sync holds a lock against Home actions. In a reproducer, a Home `link` thread ran during a 100-account catch-up sync:
     - 12 of 17 Home links that returned True were lost.
     - 3 Home links raised PermissionError (file being replaced).
     - 10 sync links were lost even though the sync reported them as placed. The next sync recovers those.

   The race existed before this PR, but the sync is a new background writer. Suggestion: compute all new rows and write them once, through one load and one `_write`. This also shrinks the race window. Also consider a module lock in account_links.
3. A links file that cannot be decoded (corrupt bytes) is caught by the outer `except`. The sync result has no `place_notes` entry, only a log line. Acceptable.
4. Spelling: "UAE" does not join an "AE" or "United Arab Emirates" group. `_known_code` has no "uae" alias, which comes from the ACL-2945 table. A lowercase map spelling ("ua", "saudi arabia") becomes the group's display name when no group exists yet. Both follow the spec.
5. `place_countries` creates `account_links.csv` when it is missing. After that, `account_links.seed_from_account_map()`, which runs lazily from Home, skips the seed because the file exists. Manual map countries on a machine that never opened Home would not be seeded. This is an edge case.
6. Accounts the buyer removed from the Available accounts list (`available_hidden.csv`, ACL-1319) are still placed under their country. Only `hidden_accounts.json` is respected. Minor.

## Verified OK
- Name variants (double spaces, case, Cf characters) match an existing placement.
- A hand link to another country is kept.
- Sync-hidden and hand-hidden accounts are skipped.
- Empty, unknown and unusable countries behave as described.
- A read-only links file gives per-account notes and the sync is still ok.
- A missing map leaves the sync ok.
- After 40 mixed accounts and three syncs (200, 304, new etag), the file is byte-identical and its mtime unchanged.
- The 2899/2901/2915 fixtures now patch `account_links.get_local_config_dir`. No test that references user_accounts lacks the patch.
- The real files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ACL and in the \localhost path were unchanged (size and mtime) before and after.
